name: Effort Result Regression Residual
note: Fits |log return| on log volume over a rolling window and trades the bars whose residual is far NEGATIVE -- enormous volume that produced almost no price change, i.e. someone absorbed the flow at a fixed price. Gated on the bar also being in the top of its own volume distribution and at least median width; the absorber's side is read off where the bar closed in its range.
source: Synthesis, built on two cited pillars: Amihud (2002), 'Illiquidity and stock returns: cross-section and time-series effects', Journal of Financial Markets 5, 31-56, https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~mkearns/finread/amihud.pdf , which establishes |return|/dollar-volume as the price response per unit of trading; and Wyckoff's effort-vs-result law as described at https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/effort-vs-result/ . The OLS-residual formulation and the clv direction rule are my own.
code:
def family_init(ctx):
    """Rolling OLS of |log return| on log volume, win bars deep, by running
    sums. The residual says how far this bar's move fell short of what its own
    volume predicts; dividing by the fit's residual sd makes the threshold
    comparable across symbols and vol regimes. A large NEGATIVE residual on a
    heavy, wide bar is Wyckoff absorption expressed as a studentised number."""
    import math
    bars = ctx.bars
    m = len(bars)
    h = [float(b["h"]) for b in bars]
    l = [float(b["l"]) for b in bars]
    c = [float(b["c"]) for b in bars]
    v = [float(b.get("v") or 0.0) for b in bars]

    W = max(30, int(ctx.p.win))
    ksd = float(ctx.p.k_sd)
    vq = float(ctx.p.vol_p)
    rq = float(ctx.p.rng_p)
    chi = float(ctx.p.clv_hi)
    clo = float(ctx.p.clv_lo)

    y = [0.0] * m                      # |log return|
    x = [0.0] * m                      # log volume
    rng = [0.0] * m                    # (h-l)/c, the bar's own width
    for i in range(m):
        vv = v[i]
        x[i] = math.log(vv) if vv > 1.0 else 0.0
        if i and c[i] > 0.0 and c[i - 1] > 0.0:
            y[i] = abs(math.log(c[i] / c[i - 1]))
        rng[i] = (h[i] - l[i]) / c[i] if c[i] > 0.0 else 0.0

    # prefix sums -> every window statistic in O(1)
    px = [0.0] * (m + 1)
    py = [0.0] * (m + 1)
    pxx = [0.0] * (m + 1)
    pyy = [0.0] * (m + 1)
    pxy = [0.0] * (m + 1)
    for i in range(m):
        px[i + 1] = px[i] + x[i]
        py[i + 1] = py[i] + y[i]
        pxx[i + 1] = pxx[i] + x[i] * x[i]
        pyy[i + 1] = pyy[i] + y[i] * y[i]
        pxy[i + 1] = pxy[i] + x[i] * y[i]

    sig = [0] * m
    n = float(W)
    for i in range(W, m):
        a0 = i - W + 1                 # window is [a0 .. i] inclusive
        b0 = i + 1
        sx = px[b0] - px[a0]
        sy = py[b0] - py[a0]
        sxx = pxx[b0] - pxx[a0]
        syy = pyy[b0] - pyy[a0]
        sxy = pxy[b0] - pxy[a0]
        Sxx = sxx - sx * sx / n
        if Sxx <= 1e-12:
            continue
        Sxy = sxy - sx * sy / n
        Syy = syy - sy * sy / n
        b = Sxy / Sxx
        a = (sy - b * sx) / n
        sse = Syy - b * Sxy
        if sse <= 0.0:
            continue
        sde = math.sqrt(sse / (n - 2.0))
        if sde <= 0.0:
            continue
        r = y[i] - (a + b * x[i])
        if r > -ksd * sde:
            continue                   # not an absorption bar
        # only now, on the few bars that qualify, pay for the percentiles
        vi = v[i]
        ri = rng[i]
        nv = 0
        nr = 0
        for j in range(a0, i + 1):
            if v[j] <= vi:
                nv += 1
            if rng[j] <= ri:
                nr += 1
        if nv < vq * n or nr < rq * n:
            continue
        d = h[i] - l[i]
        if d <= 0.0:
            continue
        clv = (c[i] - l[i]) / d
        if clv >= chi:
            sig[i] = 1
        elif clv <= clo:
            sig[i] = -1
    ctx.sig = ctx.series(sig, "absorb")


def signal(ctx, i):
    return ctx.sig[i]
